Targets.Target: Samsung Galaxy Watch running Wear OS with the approved OpenWearSync APK and Rust JNI library.
Windows PC running the Rust receiver service and Kotlin Compose Desktop application.
Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra Wi-Fi hotspot used only as the required local network access point.

NetworkTopology.Primary: Galaxy Watch Wi-Fi client to S25 Ultra hotspot to Windows receiver on the same private local network.
NetworkTopology.Transport: Watch initiates an authenticated encrypted TCP or HTTPS session to a listening Windows receiver. Mobile internet is not required for payload transfer.
NetworkTopology.Discovery: Try bounded mDNS or Android NSD discovery where multicast works, then a saved authenticated endpoint, then a manually entered local address.
NetworkTopology.Blocker: Hotspot client isolation may prevent direct station-to-station traffic. A manual IP cannot bypass isolation; the topology result must be recorded and an alternate local network chosen if required.
NetworkTopology.Binding: Transport must use the Kotlin-selected Android Wi-Fi Network and prove that payloads do not fall back to Bluetooth or an unintended default route.

Packaging.Wear: Signed Wear OS APK containing Kotlin Compose UI, Android platform adapters, and the shared Rust NDK/JNI library.
Packaging.Windows: Signed Windows Rust receiver package with its durable registry and Kotlin Compose Desktop UI.
Packaging.Protocol: Release artifacts advertise compatible protocol and registry versions and reject incompatible peers before accepting recordings.

FirewallAndStorage.Firewall: Expose only the configured receiver port on appropriate private Windows networks; do not require a public listener or cloud service.
FirewallAndStorage.Destination: Receiver destination is user-selected, validated, and owned by the Windows service. Traversal and silent overwrite are rejected.
FirewallAndStorage.Persistence: Pairing records, receiver identity, transfer journal, durable ranges, and final fingerprints survive receiver restart within the documented storage boundary.

PairingAndUpdates.Pairing: Initial pairing displays a short user-confirmed code, establishes authenticated encrypted identity, and records the receiver pin.
PairingAndUpdates.Revocation: Windows can revoke a watch identity; subsequent status, resume, and upload requests fail closed.
PairingAndUpdates.Update: Install, update, migration, downgrade refusal, rollback behavior, and protocol compatibility are release gates for a future packaging change.
PairingAndUpdates.Keys: Protected platform storage holds identity keys; package artifacts contain no private keys or test secrets.

ReleaseGates.Gate: Real Galaxy Watch build reads a Samsung Voice Recorder file without root or ADB privileges.
Watch reaches Windows through the S25 Ultra hotspot or the documented approved local topology.
Windows Firewall and destination permissions remain private and bounded.
Pairing, revocation, reconnect, receiver restart, disk-full, corruption, and atomic finalization evidence is retained.
Wear and Windows packages install, negotiate compatible versions, and clean up all session resources.
Matched battery and temperature trials confirm the approved idle and session budgets before production release.

OpenReleaseDecisions.Decision: Minimum Wear OS and Windows versions.
Distribution channel, signing identity, update cadence, and migration policy.
Exact receiver port, destination defaults, chunk budget, session duration, and supported concurrent sessions.
